title: Six species omissions can reverse the mean diet contrast in five bird drought samples from a 2024 release
abstract: We tested the sensitivity of five bird drought diet contrasts to species omission. We used 119 released rows and 99 study-species units from a 2024 public archive. Exact bounds retain at least one insect-eating and one seed-eating species in each study and hold retained responses fixed. One omission can reverse the sign in Hawaii and one Australian sample. Four omissions are needed in southeast Australia and eleven in western Australia. The North Dakota sign cannot reverse under this rule. The equal-study mean is -0.286 source effect-size units. Every set of at most five omissions keeps it negative, with an upper bound of -0.002. Six omissions permit a positive value of +0.048. These are sharp fixed-data bounds, not confidence intervals or measured selection rates. The threshold can change with response errors, missing species or a different weighting rule. Shared droughts, different methods, detection and publication selection limit inference. This secondary analysis adds a species-selection audit to a prior campaign contrast. It does not test a causal diet effect, air pollution or independent early and late periods. Code, aggregate evidence, a figure and external retrieval instructions are included.

display.caption: Exact lower and upper contrast bounds under species omission. Retained responses are fixed and each diet remains present. Shading is not a confidence interval; intermediate values need not all be attainable.
